supporting_observations.claim: WS-TWEBER-01 repeatedly made proxied HTTPS CONNECT requests to update.medledger.co from 13:36:39 through 14:06:35 UTC, at roughly five-minute intervals; one attempt returned 503 and the others shown returned 200.
The recurring requests are associated with medledgerupd.exe running from tom.weber's AppData\Local directory, rather than the inventory-approved C:\Program Files\MediLedger\medledgerupd.exe path.
The observed destination is update.medledger.co, whereas the inventory identifies update.medledger.com as MediLedger's approved update service.

The proxy records identify the requests as browser-like Chrome traffic, while endpoint network telemetry associates the corresponding proxy connections with medledgerupd.exe; this mismatch adds suspicion but does not by itself prove maliciousness.

known_telemetry_limitations: The proxy records show CONNECT tunnels and endpoint connections to the explicit proxy; the available evidence does not show the HTTPS request or response contents.
The supplied records do not establish the executable's hash, digital-signature status, provenance, or whether it was legitimately installed or replaced.
The supplied records do not establish the destination domain's ownership, DNS resolution, certificate details, or whether update.medledger.co is an authorized alias.
The visible recurring requests begin at 13:36:39 UTC; the supplied records do not show a corresponding request at the alert's stated 13:30 start.
claims_not_established: The evidence does not establish what data, if any, was sent or received through the HTTPS tunnels.
The evidence does not establish that update.medledger.co is controlled by an attacker or that the application performed a malicious update.
The evidence does not establish whether the AppData copy of medledgerupd.exe is a legitimate version, a replaced executable, or a separately installed application.
additional_evidence_needed: Collect and preserve the medledgerupd.exe file and determine its hash, signature, origin, installation time, and relationship to the approved MediLedger installation.
Validate update.medledger.co against MediLedger vendor documentation and inspect DNS, certificate, proxy, and firewall records for its destination and reputation.
Obtain proxy TLS inspection or application-level logs, if available, to determine the contents and purpose of the repeated requests and any returned update artifacts.
Review endpoint file, persistence, and process-creation history around the updater's start and exit, including any files it downloaded or modified.
unrelated_findings: Tom Weber launched OpenSSH to connect to PROXY-PIN-01; remote access is not approved from this workstation in the supplied environment context. Investigate separately. (T085-00050, T085-00051, T085-00052)

Tom Weber ran sqlcmd to attempt a database backup to D:\Backups\webapp_prod.bak on 10.0.2.50; the connection attempt to port 1433 is recorded. Investigate separately. (T085-00083, T085-00085, T085-00086)

Google Drive File Stream was launched on WS-TWEBER-01, although no non-Microsoft cloud-storage service is approved in the supplied context. Investigate separately. (T085-00282, T085-00283, T085-00284)

An unlisted Meridian OpsAgent ran as SYSTEM on WS-TWEBER-01 and attempted explicit authentication as svc-billing; the inventory describes svc-billing as the BillingSync service account on FILE-PIN-01. Investigate separately. (T085-00386, T085-00387, T085-00388)
